takeaway: Cornucopia Reloaded uses CHERI page-level load barriers to move stale-pointer cleanup off the stop-the-world path, sharply shortening heap-revocation pauses on Morello.
background: CHERI capabilities attach bounds and integrity to C and C++ pointers, providing reference integrity and spatial safety. Heap temporal safety additionally needs stale capabilities removed before freed storage is reused.
villain: Cornucopia's concurrent sweeper still had to stop every application thread and rescan redirtied pages, producing pauses too long for interactive workloads.
approach: Reloaded briefly stops threads at a revocation epoch's start to toggle a per-page capability-load generation and scan registers plus kernel-held capabilities. During the concurrent phase, capability loads from old-generation pages trap and self-heal that page while a background thread sweeps the rest; improved capability-dirty tracking prevents unnecessary rescans. It requires CHERI pure-capability userspace, a cooperating allocator and kernel, and Morello or CHERI-RISC-V-style per-page load-barrier hardware.
impact: The authors argue that Reloaded broadens deterministic heap use-after-reallocation mitigation to more latency-sensitive CHERI workloads without adding aggregate cost over Cornucopia.

evaluation.overview: The CheriBSD implementation was compared with reimplemented Cornucopia and CHERIvoke on eight pure-capability SPEC CPU2006 INT programs, PostgreSQL pgbench, and gRPC QPS; SPEC cases that never invoked revocation were excluded from detailed analysis.
evaluation.implemented: A CheriBSD kernel revoker with per-PTE capability-load generations and capability-dirty bits, plus LD_PRELOAD shims using snmalloc and mrs to quarantine freed heap objects.
evaluation.setting: Experiments used a four-core 2.5 GHz Arm Morello system, pure-capability CHERI C/C++ applications, and a spatially safe no-revocation baseline, with applications and revokers pinned to separate cores where possible; pgbench ran 170,000 transactions, while the gRPC scenario used a tuned two-thread server with transport security disabled.
baselines: Spatially safe CHERI/CheriBSD with snmalloc and no revocation
CHERIvoke derived from the Cornucopia reimplementation
Paint+sync quarantine and bitmap overhead without temporal safety

results.text: Across the revoking SPEC workloads, the authors report no additional wall-clock or CPU-time cost over Cornucopia and median bus traffic equal to 87% of Cornucopia's.
In gRPC, mean stop-the-world time fell to 0.3 ± 0.1 ms from Cornucopia's 8.7 ± 0.8 ms, while throughput reductions were statistically indistinguishable at 12.82 ± 0.16% versus 12.88 ± 0.16%.

limitations: This is deterministic use-after-reallocation mitigation, not immediate use-after-free prevention: a freed object may remain accessible while quarantined until a later revocation epoch, and correctness assumes the allocator and revocation-bitmap boundary. The evaluation shim bypassed bitmap capability access controls, the tested implementation had unexercised alias-handling defects, and very-high-percentile gRPC latency remained pathological.
phd_group_signal: The work combines security-invariant reasoning, ISA and page-table changes, deep kernel integration, allocator policy, and tail-latency experiments rather than reporting throughput alone.

claims.text: At each epoch Reloaded toggles an in-core capability-load generation, scans register and kernel-held capabilities, and then lets old-generation page loads trap and clean pages while a background thread completes the sweep; this depends on per-page capability-load generation hardware implemented by Morello and specified for CHERI-RISC-V.

Reloaded guarantees removal of capabilities to objects freed before the current revocation epoch before reuse; it may still permit access to a freed, quarantined object until a subsequent epoch, so it closes use-after-reallocation rather than the entire use-after-free window.

The design assumes protected allocator access to the revocation bitmap, but the evaluation shims bypassed that access control; the evaluated implementation also had aliased-page defects that the benchmarks did not exercise.

The experiments used a four-core 2.5 GHz Morello system and eight pure-capability SPEC programs; pgbench ran 170,000 transactions, and the gRPC server used two threads with transport security disabled.
